name: Klint Kubiak

views.text: Build the offense around the quarterback: open receivers, help in protection and room to extend plays.
Teach in long meetings first, so players carry a lot of information onto the field.
A good start is no reason to feel satisfied; stay hungry.
Pressure in a winning program is healthy if you show up with backup plans and real reasons for your ideas.
Correct the mistake where everyone can learn from it, and praise it the same way when it is earned.
Players should enjoy the game and celebrate; the standard and the fun are not opposites.

signatures: answers in short, direct sentences and steers away from talking about himself
describes himself through his job, his faith and being a father
credits the head coach who opened his game-planning meetings to him
want: to show he is a play-caller in his own right, not just a famous coaching son and brother
fear: that the early fireworks fade and he is judged only by a collapsing season around him
voice: Reserved, brief and focused; he gives short answers and little of himself to reporters. Players describe a demanding thinker who corrects in front of the group and praises when earned. When he does open up, it is about faith, family and the work.

evidence.publisher: Saints Wire (USA Today) via Yahoo Sports, John Sigler
evidence.summary: He calls his year under Shanahan eye-opening: the head coach shared his reasoning in game-plan meetings, was demanding, and the pressure was useful if coaches had backup plans; the main lesson was building around the quarterback. Earlier called plays for Minnesota (2021) and briefly Denver (2022).

evidence.publisher: WVUE Fox 8 via WLOX, Sean Fazende
evidence.summary: Offseason piece: he teaches through long meeting time, praises Carr's intelligence and says he exceeded expectations, but tells players to stay hungry and never satisfied. Local TV report.
Allen replaced Payton-era coordinator Carmichael with Kubiak and installed a new scheme, part of a staff Allen chose himself. Shows the hire, not the working relationship in depth.
In his New Orleans play-calling debut the Saints score on their first nine possessions in a 47-10 win; Kamara ties the result to the changes made. Kubiak is not quoted.

Team-site profile: reserved with media, short answers, describes himself by job, faith and fatherhood; Carr says he loves football, demands a lot and corrects mistakes in front of peers but praises when earned; Kamara calls him a constant schemer. 91 points in the first two games.

evidence.publisher: Sports Illustrated (49ers On SI), Grant Cohn
evidence.summary: His younger brother Klay, taking over Klint's 49ers pass game role, says it is the same job Klint held and that the two worked very closely together. Klay's account.
